body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The HTML table contains 14 columns with highly variable content lengths (e.g., short boolean badges vs. long inspection prompts and multiple stacked runtime blockers). Using `table-layout: fixed` without explicit column widths forces the browser to distribute the space equally among all columns. This results in severe text wrapping and excessive vertical stretching for long-text columns, while leaving short-text columns with unnecessary empty space. Changing `table-layout` to `auto` allows the browser to dynamically allocate column widths based on content, significantly improving readability.
